chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
"Whoever reaches al-Mash'ar al-Haram with five people has indeed attained hajj."

key_terms.أَدْرَكَ: reached or attained in a legally consequential sense
key_terms.خَمْسَةٍ: five, indicating the specific number mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.ٱلنَّاسِ: people or individuals present with whom this state is realized
key_terms.ٱلْحَجَّ: hajj, the pilgrimage whose attainment is being ruled upon
key_terms.ٱلْمَشْعَرَ ٱلْحَرَامَ: al-Mash'ar al-Haram, the sacred site connected to the rites of hajj

ai.seo_question: When is a person considered to have attained hajj according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal criterion related to the validity of hajj by linking its attainment to reaching al-Mash'ar al-Haram within a specified circumstance. It belongs to the jurisprudence of hajj timings and clarifies when a person is considered to have successfully attained the pilgrimage.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2773 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"Whoever reaches al-Mash'ar al-Haram (the Sacred Monument) with five individuals has indeed attained Hajj."
